name: E. Chapin, millinery and dress making

proprietors.name: Eliza Chapin
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Eliza Chapin is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at milliner in the west division (slot trade_households:persons/female/30_39/west/family/trade:milliner:006), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. Here the head is not merely the proprietor of the house — the head IS what bought it, because no count of this class was ever printed to be short of.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a millinery kept by a west-division household deals this house onto Canal Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because the resident band drew a milliner the town was short of, and the trade names the house he keeps. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. The head who keeps it is ordered onto the scene date and to nothing narrower, and a keeping is not an opening; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read yankee: Eliza Chapin (yankee). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real millinery in the west division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn with the head.

trade_head.note: A TRADE HEAD, NOT A SHORTFALL AND NOT A ROOF. The December 1835 State census's eighteen lines never reach this class, so the order book holds no bucket to point at and no count of it can be short; and nothing in data/structures/ is a millinery, so there is no committed building to buy the firm either. What IS committed is the man: the resident band drew Eliza Chapin at milliner because the 1839 trade table says the town was short of the trade, and a millinery is a shop front, and the register prints three of them at the scene date — Elmira Fowler on Dearborn Street, Mrs. H. Sherman and [Mrs.] Herman at the Mansion House — all under the one trade line 'millinery and dress making', against a census with no line for a milliner. The house is withdrawn with the head.

basis.note: the resident band drew 2 head(s) at milliner in the west division and a millinery is a shop front, and the register prints three of them at the scene date — Elmira Fowler on Dearborn Street, Mrs. H. Sherman and [Mrs.] Herman at the Mansion House — all under the one trade line 'millinery and dress making', against a census with no line for a milliner. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: form 1 of the naming guide, the corpus's commonest signature — and the form 'Mrs. H. Sherman' prints once the honorific is cut, which this programme cuts everywhere (docs/LIBERTIES.md § L257). The goods line is that line whole, as Elmira Fowler, Mrs. H. Sherman and [Mrs.] Herman all print it.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: the retirement of the head himself, a re-cut of the order book that no longer orders his person bucket, or a source naming a real house of this class; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
